product.amstrad-alt-386sx.summary: The 386SX ALT with twice the hard drive capacity in the initial configuration.
product.amstrad-alt-386sx.history: Amstrad introduced the ALT-386SX at CeBIT in March 1990 as the higher-end ALT model. Micro News reported a planned June release in France at 20,900 francs before tax. In July 1991, Amstrad Germany offered it with a portable Canon BJ-10e printer for 5,550 marks.
product.amstrad-alt-386sx.technical.stor: Some units had more storage than the manual specifies. Amstrad lists 40 MB and Pawel Pieczul documented an 80 MB Sony SRD3080C-50 set to BIOS disk type 24.
product.amstrad-alt-386sx.technical.bios: The preserved BIOS identifies itself as AMSTRAD ALT-386SX and Phoenix 1.10. It is reconstructed by interleaving U302 at even bytes and U303 at odd bytes. The reset vector jumps to F000:E05B.
product.amstrad-alt-386sx.technical.veri: The system BIOS hashes and model identity were verified through static inspection. The BluMach sheet remains in research.
product.amstrad-alt-386sx.technical.limi: The dump came from a faulty machine. A second unit is needed for comparison, along with the U508 video ROM and validation of boot and LCD control in BluMach.
